instructions: Mean-field VI exhibits anti-convergence on gp_regression: ELBO decreases monotonically over 10k Adam steps rather than increasing toward the true posterior. The d=203 latent space (3 hyperparameters + 200 inducing-point latents) and the Cholesky-factored GP likelihood create a posterior with strong inter-dimensional correlations that a diagonal Gaussian cannot approximate. The mean-field independence assumption is structurally incompatible with the GP posterior geometry.
workflow: Phase 8B.2 probe (2026-06-03, @statistician). Probe: standalone Python at num_optimization_steps=10_000, optax.adam(1e-2). ELBO trajectory shows anti-convergence (decreasing) — the mean-field approximation diverges from the posterior rather than converging. Root cause: GP regression posterior is dominated by the dense Cholesky Gram matrix, creating non-separable correlations across all 203 dimensions. A diagonal Gaussian (mean-field) assigns independent uncertainty to correlated latents, causing the optimizer to chase contradictory gradient signals. Full-rank VI (d=203 >> 30 Cat 8 threshold) is also excluded by Cat 8. Classification: out_of_scope (structural incompatibility, not a tuning failure).
